data: 1970s NASA outer-planet workhorse — Centaur D-1A's first H₂ upper stage opened the gas giants

Stretched Atlas booster (the 'Atlas SLV-3D') with the LOX/LH₂ Centaur D-1A — the world's first hydrogen-fuelled upper stage, and the key enabler of every American Jupiter / Saturn / Helios / Mariner mission of the 1970s. Replaced the earlier SLV-3C in 1973, served through 1983 (last flight Intelsat V F-7), and was itself superseded by the Atlas G/H/I family that fed into the Atlas II of the 1990s. The Star-37E or Star-48 solid-kick stage was bolted on top for the very-high-energy trajectories that sent Pioneer 11 past Jupiter to a Saturn rendezvous.

1970s NASA outer-planet workhorse — Pioneer 10/11, Helios 1/2, Mariner 9/10, Pioneer Venus

Stretched Atlas SLV-3D first stage with the world's first hydrogen-fuelled upper stage (Centaur D-1A, LOX/LH₂) — the combination that enabled every American Jupiter, Saturn, Mariner, and Helios mission of the 1970s. A Star-37E or Star-48 solid-kick stage was added on top for the very-high-energy trajectories (Pioneer 11 past Jupiter to Saturn). Served 1973-1983; superseded by the Atlas G/H/I family that fed into the Atlas II of the 1990s.
First spacecraft to fly past Saturn (1979-09-01); demonstrated the gravity-assist that sent Voyager 2 onward
First Mercury flyby; first dual-planet flyby; first gravity-assist mission
First spacecraft to encounter Saturn — Jupiter flyby in 1974 then gravity-assist to Saturn in 1979
USAF Atlas-Centaur pad — Mariner 10, Pioneer 11 (1973), Pioneer Venus (1978); now Blue Origin New Glenn (leased 2015, flew 2025)
Lifted Apollo 7, Skylab crews, and ASTP
First US human-rated launcher — variant of the Army's Redstone IRBM. Launched Freedom 7 (1961-05-05) and Liberty Bell 7 (1961-07-21)
